requirement: Avoid re-downloading unchanged JSON resources by storing each response's ETag and sending conditional requests, serving the cached body when the server answers 304 Not Modified.
skeleton: A frozen cache entry dataclass and an EtagCache with a per-URL dict, get_json sending If-None-Match, returning the cached body on 304, raising on errors, and replacing or dropping the entry based on the new ETag.
caption: A small HTTP cache over requests that revalidates JSON resources with ETags. EtagCache(session, *, timeout=10.0) keeps a per-URL dict of frozen entries holding the ETag and parsed body, plus a revalidated counter. get_json(url) sends If-None-Match with the stored ETag exactly as received when an entry exists. A 304 with an entry increments revalidated and returns the cached body. Otherwise raise_for_status turns errors into requests.HTTPError before the cache is touched, so the old entry survives. A 200 body is parsed; when the response has an ETag the entry is replaced with the new tag and body, and when it has none the entry is dropped. The fixture asserts, against a local server, that a second fetch sends the quoted v1 tag and is served from cache, that a changed resource replaces the entry so the next request sends v2, that URLs cache separately, that a response without an ETag drops the entry, and that a 500 raises requests.HTTPError while keeping the entry.

constraints: If-None-Match carries the stored ETag verbatim
Errors raise requests.HTTPError and keep the entry
A new ETag replaces the entry
A response without ETag drops the entry

rationale.teaches: Use If-None-Match with the opaque ETag, treat 304 as a cache hit, and keep the cache consistent by replacing or evicting on every successful response.
rationale.why: Keeping a stale tag forces full downloads forever, re-quoting the tag never matches, and caching error bodies serves failures as data.

ops.docstring: Cache JSON GET responses and revalidate them with ETags.

candidates.why_wrong: The ETag is sent as If-Modified-Since, so the server never answers 304.
An existing entry is never updated, so revalidation keeps sending the old tag.
An entry survives a response without ETag and is revalidated with a stale tag.
A 500 error body is returned and evicts the cached entry.
The already quoted ETag is wrapped in extra quotes and never matches.
